about: REDUNDANCY-02 hand-kept half of the exit infrastructure map. scripts/exit-map.mjs joins it with what the code actually uses and writes docs/engineering/EXIT_INFRASTRUCTURE_MAP.md. Owners must be registry calls. Prices are deliberately absent: they are unverified until COST_OPERATIONS supplies dated quotes.

exits.A: Self-hosted Supabase on owned cloud servers (AWS EC2 or Azure VM). Same service interfaces; the app changes only its URL and keys. Recommended exit (PORTABILITY, HOSTING_DECISION_BRIEF).
exits.B: Cloud-native services (managed PostgreSQL plus provider Auth, object storage, messaging and functions). New adapters behind lib/; a separate project, used only if exit A is ruled out.

components.name: PostgreSQL database (tables, RLS, functions, triggers, sequences)
components.today: Supabase managed Postgres

exitA.aws: Supabase Postgres image on EC2 with encrypted EBS gp3 data volume
exitA.azure: Supabase Postgres image on a Linux VM with encrypted Premium SSD

exitB.aws: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL or Aurora PostgreSQL
exitB.azure: Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server

components.notes: Exit B must recreate the Supabase roles (anon, authenticated, service_role), auth.uid()/auth.role()/auth.jwt() and the JWT-claims session settings RLS reads, or every policy fails closed.

exitA.azure: PostgREST container in the self-hosted stack

exitB.azure: PostgREST container on Azure Container Apps, or an API layer behind lib/

components.notes: 2026-10-21 local media transport: lib/mediaStorage.ts binds upload/public URL/sign/list/remove; lib/media.ts resolves public references and legacy URLs, with authorized Vault signing. MediaUploadService factories and photo cleanup accept bound adapters; current Supabase remains default. Full-URL writers/backfill remain gated. Alternate hosts must preserve actor authorization, exact object paths, Storage catalog/owner metadata, SQL cleanup protocol and physical byte removal; no hosted restore/parity/drill is established by local adapter tests. See design/MEDIA_SERVICE_PLAN.md.

exitA.azure: VNet with the same subnet split across 2 zones; NAT Gateway; NSGs

exitB.aws: Same VPC layout; RDS in private subnets; VPC endpoints for S3 and Secrets Manager

components.today: Supabase-managed (no app load balancer; app not hosted)

exitA.azure: Azure Front Door (Standard/Premium) caching the same paths; SAS for private objects

exitB.aws: CloudFront in front of S3
exitB.azure: Front Door in front of Blob Storage

components.name: Web application firewall, DDoS protection and rate limits
components.today: Supabase-managed edge protections; app-level caps in SQL

exitA.aws: AWS WAF on CloudFront and the ALB (managed rule groups, per-IP rate rules on /auth/v1 and guest RPCs); AWS Shield Standard (Advanced optional)
exitA.azure: Front Door WAF policy with managed and rate-limit rules; Azure DDoS Network Protection on the VNet

exitB.aws: Same
exitB.azure: Same

components.notes: Rate rules must cover sign-in, sign-up, password reset and the guest-callable cast_cheer_vote / increment_player_hype (known stuffing gap, WORK_QUEUE DATA-01-F11).

components.name: Cache server (Redis-compatible)
components.today: None (the app reads the database directly; offline queue is on the device)

exitA.aws: Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey/Redis in private subnets
exitA.azure: Azure Cache for Redis in the VNet

exitB.aws: ElastiCache Serverless
exitB.azure: Azure Cache for Redis

components.notes: Not needed for a like-for-like move. First uses when load requires it: WAF-independent rate-limit counters, short-TTL caches of public reads (feed, leaderboards, live scores) behind the API layer, Realtime fan-out relief. Never cache RLS-scoped or private rows under a shared key; invalidate on writes; the app must behave identically with the cache empty.

components.name: Database connection pooler
components.today: Supabase Supavisor / PgBouncer

exitA.aws: Supavisor (part of the self-hosted stack) or PgBouncer on the database host
exitA.azure: Supavisor or PgBouncer on the database host

exitB.aws: RDS Proxy (or PgBouncer on ECS)
exitB.azure: Flexible Server built-in PgBouncer

components.notes: Transaction pooling breaks session-level settings; the app sets JWT claims per transaction (PostgREST), which is compatible. Admin/migration jobs connect directly.

components.name: Database high availability, replicas and point-in-time recovery
components.today: Supabase-managed backups (plan-dependent PITR)

exitA.aws: Primary plus streaming standby in a second AZ (Patroni or repmgr), WAL archiving to S3 (wal-g / pgBackRest) for PITR; or move the database tier to exit B
exitA.azure: Primary plus standby VM in a second zone, WAL archive to Blob; or move the database tier to exit B

exitB.aws: RDS Multi-AZ (or Aurora) with automated backups/PITR; one read replica for reports
exitB.azure: Flexible Server zone-redundant HA with PITR; read replica

components.notes: Self-run HA is the hardest part of exit A; a managed database (exit B tier) with the self-hosted Supabase services pointed at it is a valid hybrid. Replicas must be read-only for app writes; reports can read them.

components.name: Migration data movement (dump/restore or online replication)
components.today: Not applicable

exitA.aws: Default: quiesced pg_dump → reviewed pg_restore → grant-sync → parity + access PASS. Online option: native logical replication (publication on Supabase → subscription on target) or AWS DMS
exitA.azure: Same default; online option: logical replication or Azure Database Migration Service (online)

exitB.aws: Same default; AWS DMS (full load + CDC) for online
exitB.azure: Same default; Azure DMS online

components.notes: Logical replication does not carry DDL, sequences, auth/storage service schemas or large objects: freeze schema changes, setval sequences at cutover, and copy Storage objects separately (bulk pre-copy, delta during the freeze).

components.today: Clients call the supabase.co project URL compiled into each build

exitA.azure: Azure DNS with Traffic Manager or Front Door routing

exitB.aws: Same
exitB.azure: Same

components.notes: Do this well before any exit: give clients an endpoint we control (Supabase custom domain, or our own api domain proxying to Supabase) and ship builds that use it. Then cutover is a DNS change, not an app release, and old installs follow automatically. Owner decision (paid add-on or proxy).

migrationStrategies.name: Freeze and restore (default at current size)
migrationStrategies.how: Freeze all writers → final quiesced encrypted backup → reviewed Auth data preload if required → historical Storage bytes before app guards → owner reconciliation → reviewed main DB restore → grant-sync → complete database/Storage/service/client/finance parity → one owned gateway route → reopen
migrationStrategies.downtime: Owner target2–3hours on a prepared target; unmeasured. Complete warm rehearsal≤180minutes required
migrationStrategies.rollback: Keep source frozen; route owned stable gateway back through independently tested session/client policy. Reconcile all target writes before reopening either side
migrationStrategies.when: Default while the database is small

migrationStrategies.name: Online replication (near-zero downtime)
migrationStrategies.how: Initial copy + continuous change capture from Supabase (native logical replication or AWS DMS / Azure DMS) while the app keeps running; short freeze only to drain the last changes, set sequences, verify parity + access, switch DNS
migrationStrategies.rollback: Reverse replication target → Supabase prepared before cutover, or freeze-and-restore back
migrationStrategies.when: When the database is too large to dump within an acceptable window; needs schema-change freeze, primary keys or replica identity on every replicated table, and separate handling of auth/storage schemas, sequences and Storage objects

protection.azure: Key Vault-managed keys for disks/Postgres/Blob; backups age-encrypted
protection.why: Minor, guardian, Auth and finance data

protection.aws: TLS 1.2+ at CloudFront/ALB; verify-full to the database
protection.azure: TLS 1.2+ at Front Door/App Gateway; verify-full to the database

protection.aws: Private subnets, security groups, VPC endpoints
protection.why: Database and admin ports unreachable from the internet

protection.aws: AWS WAF managed + rate rules, Shield
protection.azure: Front Door WAF, DDoS Network Protection
protection.why: Auth abuse, scraping, guest vote stuffing, floods

protection.aws: IAM roles per service, GitHub OIDC, no long-lived keys
protection.why: A leaked credential cannot reach everything
Keys known to the old provider are retired
A raw restore reopened 2,059 revoked rights; access parity proves each user sees the same rows

protection.aws: Database read-only roles on Supabase during the final copy
protection.why: No write lost between snapshot and switch

protection.aws: Encrypted archive in two accounts/clouds; readback verified
protection.why: Rollback and disaster recovery do not depend on the migration succeeding
Every operator action and failure is visible

protection.aws: Supabase frozen, intact, DNS switch-back rehearsed
protection.why: A failed cutover returns users to the known-good system
